object_description: high compact volume with a symmetrical shade roof and split-level base
design_condition: The high, compact volume is placed centrally and parallel to the surrounding high-rise blocks, preserving the existing flowing outdoor space while remaining autonomous from the primary school complex.

positive.statement: The high structure allows a small footprint and preserves the flowing outdoor space.
The structural order gives the design its quality.
The two central staircases create well-proportioned access halls as anterooms to the classrooms.
The slope of the terrain is cleverly used to illuminate the gymnasium and create ground-floor zoning.
The division of the canteens according to age groups makes sense.
The concrete support plate structure allows great flexibility.
The architectural expression with structurally modern themes is convincing in the context of the surrounding buildings.

negative.statement: The large asphalted break area and all-weather area create a strong contrast to the flowing green space.
The poorly designed surroundings and large hard-surface areas do not use the urban-development potential sufficiently.
The shade roof limits the quality of stay.
The excavation required to illuminate the gymnasium may seem forced.
The kitchen cannot be optimally arranged for both canteens, and meal distribution is constrained.
Views over the district and vertical spatial relationships between floors would make the climb easier.
Individual group rooms and offices are too narrow.
The basement workshops have only indirect lighting and are unlikely to be eligible for approval.
Access to the basement floors, workshops and cloakrooms is too small and not sufficiently generous.
The height, solitary urban setting and architectural expression were questioned for the expanded school complex.
